title: Decode: KDA core (FP32 state)
shape: D3-32 r24: 96 requests / DP rank (384 verify rows), L≈135K, k=3; per GPU 24 KDA heads x 96 requests = 2304 (request, head) items/layer
gap_analysis: KdaWide 30-49 us/layer vs model 8.8 (B32) / 26.3 (B96) us/layer. Model achievable is memory bound: per (request, head) item 64 KB FP32 state read + 64 KB write (deferred fold writes the committed checkpoint once) + ~14 KB conv window + records, at the measured full-chip default-allocation HBM rate. Hypotheses (unmeasured): (1) per-item CTA grid keeps too few state bytes in flight per SM (one 64 KB page per CTA, 2 CTAs/SM, load -> compute -> store serialized), (2) FP32 recurrence work per item (~0.8 MFLOP) is ~55% of the memory time, so compute must overlap with streaming, (3) above n=70 KdaWS is used and it does NOT fold: the step pays a separate flush (state read + write) plus a read in KdaWS = 3 state passes instead of 2. Measurement (baseline microbench + ncu) is next.
inefficiencies: HYPOTHESIS: latency-bound per-(head, request) CTA grid: few state bytes in flight per SM
HYPOTHESIS: KdaWS (n>=71) does not fold the deferred commit: separate flush = 3 state passes instead of 2
HYPOTHESIS: die-oblivious state streaming: half the bytes cross the die-to-die link (default 4 KiB die interleave)
Two kernels across batch sizes (KdaWide <=70, KdaWS above)
rubin_features: two-die locality domains: per-4 KiB page home die (default interleave) + %smid -> die map (dies.py)
bulk async copies (TMA) into a multi-stage shared-memory ring
